public_rationale: In July 2024 Zitron forecast that generative AI will not become AGI or science-fiction-style AI. He gave no deadline. The only evidence item is an April 2026 post by Simon Willison (e1). It quotes an October 2025 OpenAI statement that any AGI declaration by OpenAI would be verified by an independent expert panel. The post does not report any such declaration or panel ruling. So the cited evidence does not show a generative-AI system independently verified or broadly accepted as AGI, which is what the contract needs for contradiction. The evidence also shows no decisive finding that generative AI cannot reach AGI, which is what the contract needs for support. With no deadline, a lack of AGI so far cannot confirm the forecast. The claim stays open.
limitations: AGI has no agreed definition, and 'science-fiction' AI has no measurable standard. Any future resolution will depend on which definition is used.
The evidence item covers events up to April 2026. It does not show the state of any AGI declaration or panel review between then and the evaluation date.
The packet does not assess informal public statements that AGI has arrived. None of these is a verified determination.

our_interpretation: Read as a forecast with no deadline that generative-AI systems (LLM-based) will never reach human-level general intelligence, nor become sci-fi-style assistants like Jarvis.

Plain reading: the forecast fails if a generative-AI-based system becomes widely accepted (for example, through independent expert verification or broad expert consensus) as general human-level intelligence.
criteria.support_condition: Can only be confirmed for good if the generative-AI paradigm is widely abandoned or shown not to lead to AGI. With no deadline, continued absence of AGI does not settle it.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A generative-AI-based system is widely accepted as AGI, for example through verification by the independent expert panel in the Microsoft–OpenAI agreement or broad expert consensus.
